options.en: Nothing — the first crew had more time with her, so their label should stand
options.zh: 没问题——前一组和她接触的时间更长，他们的标签应该沿用

options.en: Diagnostic momentum — restart from the primary survey; this fits PE
options.zh: 诊断惯性——从初级评估重新开始；这些表现符合肺栓塞

options.en: Availability bias — panic attacks are too rare to have been considered
options.zh: 可得性偏倚——惊恐发作太罕见，不该被考虑

options.en: Sunk-cost fallacy — the first crew's effort should not be wasted
options.zh: 沉没成本谬误——前一组花的功夫不能浪费

questions.explanationEn: Diagnostic momentum is the tendency for a label to gather force each time it is handed on, until it is treated as fact without anyone re-checking the evidence. Anxiety is a diagnosis of exclusion, and this patient has objective findings that anxiety does not produce — hypoxia, pleuritic pain, tachycardia — plus a major risk factor for venous thromboembolism. The right move is to receive the handover politely, then do your own primary survey and vital signs: oxygen to SpO₂ ≥94%, position of comfort, 12-lead, and a transport decision based on what you find (respiratory distress and hypoxia are unstable criteria). Deferring to the first crew is the error, not the remedy; panic attacks are common, so availability is not the problem; and sunk cost is about reluctance to abandon one's own investment.
questions.explanationZh: 诊断惯性是指一个标签每经一次传递就更有分量，直到没人再核对证据就把它当成事实。焦虑是排除性诊断，而这位患者有焦虑解释不了的客观发现——低氧、胸膜性胸痛、心动过速——再加上静脉血栓栓塞的重大危险因素。正确做法是礼貌地接下交接，然后自己做初级评估和生命体征：给氧到 SpO₂ ≥94%、舒适体位、12 导联，并根据自己的发现做转运决定（呼吸窘迫和低氧都是不稳定标准）。顺从前一组的判断是错误本身，不是补救；惊恐发作很常见，所以问题不在可得性；沉没成本说的是舍不得放弃自己已投入的东西。

questions.questionEn: Which statement about dual-process (System 1 / System 2) thinking in clinical decision-making is correct?
questions.questionZh: 关于临床决策中的双系统思维（系统 1 / 系统 2），哪一项说法正确？

options.en: System 2 is the fast, intuitive mode that experienced crews rely on in emergencies
options.zh: 系统 2 是有经验的团队在急症中依赖的快速直觉模式

options.en: System 1 should never be used by a competent paramedic on a critical call
options.zh: 称职的急救员在危重呼叫中永远不该用系统 1

options.en: Experts rely only on System 2 analysis once they have enough experience
options.zh: 专家经验足够之后只靠系统 2 的分析

options.en: System 1 is fast pattern recognition; System 2 is slow analysis that checks it
options.zh: 系统 1 是快速模式识别；系统 2 是校验它的缓慢分析

questions.explanationEn: System 1 is intuitive, automatic and almost effortless; it lets an experienced paramedic recognize 'sick' from the doorway and run a familiar protocol smoothly. Its cost is that it works by pattern-matching, which is exactly where anchoring, availability and premature closure live. System 2 is analytical, slow and effortful, and cannot be sustained for everything. Skilled practice is not choosing one over the other but knowing when to switch: red flags, findings that do not fit, a patient who is not improving, or a deliberate check-point such as the AET course's 'What else could this be?' before the first intervention and its structured reassessment after each one. Fatigue, time pressure and cognitive overload all push people back toward System 1 — which is why checklists and a partner's cross-check matter most on the hardest calls.
questions.explanationZh: 系统 1 是直觉的、自动的、几乎不费力的；它让有经验的急救员站在门口就能认出「这人不行了」，并把熟悉的协议跑得很顺。代价是它靠模式匹配，而锚定、可得性、过早下结论恰恰就住在那里。系统 2 是分析性的、慢而费力的，不可能对每件事都用。熟练的做法不是二选一，而是知道何时切换：出现危险信号、发现对不上、患者没有好转，或者在刻意设定的检查点——比如 AET 课程要求在第一个干预前问「还可能是什么？」、每次处置后做结构化复评。疲劳、时间压力和认知超载都会把人推回系统 1——这正是清单和搭档交叉核对在最难的呼叫里最重要的原因。

questions.questionEn: After a motorcycle crash the rider has an obvious open lower-leg fracture. The crew spends eight minutes splinting it; nobody has looked at his abdomen or pelvis, and he is getting paler. Which bias is at work?
questions.questionZh: 摩托车事故后，骑手小腿有明显的开放性骨折。队员花了八分钟给它夹板固定；没有人看过他的腹部和骨盆，而他的脸色越来越白。这是哪种偏倚在作怪？

options.en: Search satisficing — finish the rapid body survey
options.zh: 搜索满足——做完快速全身检查

options.en: Anchoring to the dispatch information about a motorcycle crash
options.zh: 对「摩托车事故」这条派遣信息的锚定

options.en: Framing effect from the patient's calm, cooperative demeanour
options.zh: 患者镇定配合的神态带来的框架效应

options.en: Hindsight bias about the splinting decision
options.zh: 对夹板固定决定的后见之明偏倚

questions.explanationEn: Search satisficing (also called premature search closure) is calling off the hunt as soon as something is found — the 'we found the injury' feeling. A visually striking limb injury is the classic distractor: it is rarely what kills the patient, while the pelvis, abdomen and chest are. The BC primary survey puts the rapid body survey before any treatment of a fracture, and the grading guide marks a rapid exam that is 'insufficient to locate life/limb threatening conditions' as a 100% deficiency; a distracting injury is also a reason to maintain spinal precautions. Increasing pallor is the body telling you the search is not over. Dispatch information and demeanour are not what drove this error, and hindsight bias is about judging decisions after the outcome is known.
questions.explanationZh: 搜索满足（也叫过早结束搜索）是一找到东西就收兵——那种「伤找到了」的感觉。视觉冲击力强的肢体伤是经典的干扰项：它很少是致死原因，骨盆、腹部和胸部才是。BC 初级评估把快速全身检查排在任何骨折处理之前，评分指南把「不足以发现危及生命/肢体情况」的快速检查列为 100% 的缺陷；分散注意的伤也是维持脊柱保护的理由之一。脸色越来越白，是身体在告诉你搜索还没结束。派遣信息和患者的神态都不是这次错误的驱动因素，后见之明偏倚说的是知道结果之后再去评判当初的决定。

questions.questionEn: Two patients, a screaming family, constant radio traffic — and you realize you cannot remember whether you already gave your chest-pain patient his ASA. What is the best way to manage the overload?
questions.questionZh: 两名患者，家属在尖叫，无线电不停——你突然发现自己记不清有没有给胸痛患者吃过 ASA。应对这种超负荷的最佳方式是什么？

options.en: Work faster so you finish before you forget anything else
options.zh: 加快速度，趁还没忘更多赶紧做完

options.en: Call a brief time-out, assign your partner roles and re-anchor on a checklist
options.zh: 叫一个短暂的暂停，给搭档分配角色，用清单重新定位

options.en: Ask the family which patient to treat first, since they know them
options.zh: 让家属决定先处理谁，因为他们了解患者

options.en: Give a second ASA to be safe — it is a low-risk drug
options.zh: 保险起见再给一次 ASA——这药风险低

questions.explanationEn: Working memory holds only a few items, and under stress the first casualties are sequence and recall. The remedies taught in the AET module are external: offload tasks to a partner with explicit roles, use a written or memorized structure (the primary-survey sequence, SAMPLE, the protocol steps) so nothing depends on memory, and take a deliberate pause to rebuild the picture — the same 'time-out' used against bias. Speeding up raises the error rate. Delegating clinical priorities to distressed relatives abandons leadership. A repeat ASA is not harmless: the BC monograph lists 'patient has already taken their recommended Aspirin dose' as a contraindication, so the honest answer to 'did I give it?' has to come from the record or the partner, not from a guess.
questions.explanationZh: 工作记忆只能装下几件事，压力之下最先丢的就是顺序和回忆。AET 模块教的对策都是外部化的：把任务分给搭档并明确角色，用写下来或背熟的结构（初级评估顺序、SAMPLE、协议步骤）让一切不依赖记忆，刻意停一下重建全局——和对抗偏倚用的「暂停」是同一招。加快速度只会提高出错率。把临床优先级交给情绪崩溃的家属，等于放弃了领导。再给一次 ASA 并不无害：BC 药物专论把「患者已经服过推荐剂量的阿司匹林」列为禁忌，所以「我给过没有」的诚实答案必须来自记录或搭档，而不是猜。

questions.questionEn: In the Swiss cheese model of error, what do the holes in each slice represent?
questions.questionZh: 在差错的「瑞士奶酪模型」里，每一片奶酪上的孔代表什么？

options.en: The number of people who handled the patient at each stage of the call
options.zh: 呼叫各阶段经手患者的人数

options.en: The patient's comorbidities that made harm more likely
options.zh: 让伤害更容易发生的患者合并症

options.en: Weaknesses in each defensive layer that cause harm only when they align
options.zh: 每层防线上的薄弱点，只有排成一线时才造成伤害

options.en: Disciplinary sanctions applied to the individuals involved
options.zh: 对相关个人施加的纪律处分

questions.explanationEn: Each slice is a defence — training, protocols, equipment checks, the partner cross-check, the drug label — and none is perfect. Latent conditions are holes built into the system long before the call (an ambiguous drug label, an understaffed shift, a broken radio); active failures are the slips and mistakes of the people at the sharp end. Most of the time a hole in one layer is caught by the next; harm occurs when the holes momentarily align. The model's lesson, and the reason the AET course pairs it with Just Culture, is that fixing the system's holes prevents more harm than punishing the last person who touched the patient. The AET module uses an HFACS-style set of layers — organizational influences, unsafe supervision, preconditions for unsafe acts, and the unsafe acts themselves.
questions.explanationZh: 每一片奶酪都是一道防线——培训、协议、设备检查、搭档交叉核对、药品标签——没有一道是完美的。潜在条件是早在这通呼叫之前就埋在系统里的孔（含糊的药品标签、人手不足的班次、坏掉的对讲机）；主动失误是一线人员的失手和错误。多数时候一层的孔会被下一层挡住；只有孔在某一刻排成一线时才会造成伤害。这个模型的教训，也是 AET 课程把它和公正文化放在一起讲的原因：补系统的孔，比惩罚最后一个碰到患者的人更能防止伤害。AET 模块用的是 HFACS 式的分层——组织影响、不安全的监督、不安全行为的前提条件，以及不安全行为本身。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic in the fourteenth hour of a shift misreads a medication concentration. Using the HFACS-style layers taught in the AET module, where does the paramedic's fatigue belong?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员在当班第 14 个小时看错了药物浓度。按 AET 模块教的 HFACS 式分层，这名急救员的疲劳应归在哪一层？

options.en: An unsafe act — fatigue is itself the error that caused harm
options.zh: 不安全行为——疲劳本身就是造成伤害的差错

options.en: Unsafe supervision by the on-duty superintendent
options.zh: 值班主管的不安全监督

options.en: Organizational influence from the staffing model
options.zh: 人员配置模式带来的组织影响

options.en: A precondition for unsafe acts — the operator's state
options.zh: 不安全行为的前提条件——操作者的状态

questions.explanationEn: In the HFACS framework the misreading itself is the unsafe act (a skill-based error). Fatigue, stress, illness, poor communication and a cramped, dark workspace are preconditions — the conditions of the operator and environment that set the error up. The scheduling policy or staffing shortage that produced a fourteen-hour shift is an organizational influence, and a supervisor who knowingly left a fatigued crew on the road would be unsafe supervision. Separating the layers matters because each needs a different fix: a tired paramedic needs rest and a cross-check partner today, while the roster needs changing by the organization. For the paramedic, fitness-to-practise obligations (AET module 6A) include self-reporting when too fatigued to work safely.
questions.explanationZh: 在 HFACS 框架里，看错浓度本身是不安全行为（技能型差错）。疲劳、压力、生病、沟通不畅、狭窄昏暗的工作环境都是前提条件——为差错铺路的操作者状态和环境条件。导致 14 小时班次的排班政策或人手短缺是组织影响；明知队员疲劳还让他们继续跑车的主管则是不安全的监督。分清层次很重要，因为每一层的修法不同：疲劳的急救员今天需要休息和搭档的交叉核对，而排班表需要组织去改。对急救员本人来说，执业适格义务（AET 模块 6A）包括在疲劳到无法安全工作时主动上报。

questions.questionEn: After a salbutamol nebulizer, your asthmatic patient's wheeze is much quieter, but SpO₂ has fallen from 93% to 89% and he is drowsier. Applying the AET course's structured reassessment (what changed, what should have changed, what got worse), what is your conclusion?
questions.questionZh: 沙丁胺醇雾化之后，哮喘患者的哮鸣音安静了许多，但 SpO₂ 从 93% 降到 89%，人也更嗜睡了。用 AET 课程的结构化复评（什么变了、什么本该变、什么变差了）来看，你的结论是什么？

options.en: A silent chest — he is tiring; assist ventilation and escalate
options.zh: 沉默胸——他在耗竭；辅助通气并升级处置

options.en: The treatment worked — less wheeze means the airways are open
options.zh: 治疗起效了——哮鸣音少了说明气道通了

options.en: Repeat the nebulizer with ipratropium and reassess in 20 minutes
options.zh: 加异丙托溴铵再雾化一次，20 分钟后复评

options.en: The drowsiness is a side effect of salbutamol and will pass
options.zh: 嗜睡是沙丁胺醇的副作用，会过去的

questions.explanationEn: A reassessment that asks only 'what changed?' would record 'wheeze decreased' and stop. The structured version forces the other two questions: what should have changed (SpO₂ should have risen and work of breathing eased — neither did) and what got worse (saturation and level of consciousness). Wheeze needs airflow; when it fades while the patient deteriorates, air is no longer moving — the silent chest of impending respiratory failure. The response is to assist ventilation with a BVM, which the BC guideline indicates for 'distressed respirations' with decreasing LOC, cyanosis or falling saturations, and to request ALS while transporting urgently (respiratory distress is an unstable criterion). Salbutamol causes tremor and tachycardia, not sedation; waiting 20 minutes could be fatal.
questions.explanationZh: 只问「什么变了」的复评会记下「哮鸣音减少」然后结束。结构化版本逼你再问两个问题：什么本该变（SpO₂ 应该上升、呼吸做功应该减轻——都没有）；什么变差了（饱和度和意识水平）。哮鸣音需要有气流才发得出来；当它在患者恶化的同时消失，说明气已经不动了——这就是呼吸衰竭将至的沉默胸。应对是用 BVM 辅助通气（BC 考纲对「呼吸窘迫」伴意识下降、发绀或饱和度下降明确给出此指征），同时呼叫 ALS 并紧急转运（呼吸窘迫是不稳定标准）。沙丁胺醇引起的是震颤和心动过速，不是嗜睡；等 20 分钟可能致命。

questions.questionEn: Just Culture sorts behaviour that leads to an adverse event into three categories, each with its own response. Which pairing is correct?
questions.questionZh: 公正文化把导致不良事件的行为分为三类，每类对应不同的处理。哪一组配对正确？

options.en: Human error → disciplinary action proportionate to the harm
options.zh: 人为失误 → 与伤害程度相称的纪律处分

options.en: At-risk behaviour → coaching and removing the incentive for the shortcut
options.zh: 冒险行为 → 辅导，并消除促成捷径的诱因

options.en: Reckless behaviour → consoling the provider and fixing the system that failed
options.zh: 鲁莽行为 → 安抚当事人并修复失效的系统

options.en: Every category → mandatory retraining before return to duty
options.zh: 所有类别 → 复岗前一律强制再培训

questions.explanationEn: Human error is an unintended slip or lapse: the response is to console the person and fix the system that allowed it. At-risk behaviour is a conscious choice whose risk was not appreciated or had come to seem normal (skipping a check because 'we never have time'): the response is coaching plus changing the pressures that reward the shortcut. Reckless behaviour is a conscious disregard of a substantial, unjustifiable risk (working impaired, falsifying a record): that is the only category where discipline is the appropriate response. Punishing human error drives reporting underground and leaves the system hole open — a point worth stressing because at least one item in the AET's own quiz bank attaches 'disciplinary action' to human error in its answer key while its feedback text says the opposite.
questions.explanationZh: 人为失误是无意的失手或疏漏：处理方式是安抚当事人，并修复容许它发生的系统。冒险行为是有意识的选择，但没意识到风险或已经习以为常（因为「总是没时间」而跳过核对）：处理方式是辅导，并改变奖励捷径的那些压力。鲁莽行为是有意识地无视重大且不可辩护的风险（带着损伤状态工作、伪造记录）：只有这一类才适合纪律处分。惩罚人为失误会让上报转入地下，系统的漏洞却还敞着——这一点值得强调，因为 AET 自己题库里至少有一题的答案键把「纪律处分」配给了人为失误，而它的反馈文字说的恰恰相反。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic has, for months, skipped the second-person drug check 'because we are always short on time'. Today she draws up the wrong concentration and it is given. How does Just Culture classify this, and what should follow?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员几个月来一直跳过第二人核药，「因为我们总是赶时间」。今天她抽错了浓度，药也给出去了。公正文化怎么归类？接下来该怎么做？

options.en: Human error — console her and change nothing else
options.zh: 人为失误——安抚她，别的什么都不改

options.en: Reckless behaviour — immediate dismissal and a report to the licensing board
options.zh: 鲁莽行为——立即解雇并上报发牌机构

options.en: No category applies because the patient was not harmed by the dose
options.zh: 患者没有因这个剂量受到伤害，所以不归任何类别

options.en: At-risk behaviour — coach her, and fix the time pressure that drove the shortcut
options.zh: 冒险行为——辅导她，并解决催生这条捷径的时间压力

questions.explanationEn: The wrong concentration was a slip, but the behaviour that let it reach the patient was a deliberate, habitual shortcut whose risk had drifted out of view — the definition of at-risk behaviour. The right response addresses both the individual (coaching about why the independent check exists) and the system (why a crew feels there is never time; whether look-alike concentrations are stocked side by side). It is not reckless, because she was not knowingly accepting a substantial risk; dismissal would also teach everyone else to hide the next one. Consoling alone ignores the choice that was made. Just Culture classifies the behaviour, not the outcome — a near-miss and a fatality from the same shortcut get the same classification, which is exactly why near-misses are worth reporting.
questions.explanationZh: 抽错浓度是一次失手，但让它到达患者的，是一个有意的、习惯性的捷径，其风险早已淡出视线——这正是冒险行为的定义。正确的处理要同时面向个人（辅导她理解独立核对为什么存在）和系统（为什么一组人总觉得没时间；相似浓度的药是不是并排摆放）。这不算鲁莽，因为她并非明知有重大风险还接受；解雇还会教会其他人把下一次藏起来。只安抚则忽略了她做出的那个选择。公正文化归类的是行为，不是结果——同一个捷径造成的险肇事件和死亡事件归类相同，这也正是险肇事件值得上报的原因。

questions.questionEn: You pick up an ampoule, and your partner's cross-check catches that it is a different drug in nearly identical packaging. Nothing was given. What should happen now?
questions.questionZh: 你拿起一支安瓿，搭档交叉核对时发现那是另一种药、包装几乎一模一样。药没有给出去。接下来该怎么做？

options.en: Set it aside, re-check and draw up the right drug, and report the near-miss
options.zh: 把它放到一边，重新核对后抽正确的药，并上报险肇事件

options.en: Say nothing — no harm was done, so there is nothing to report
options.zh: 什么都不说——没造成伤害，就没什么好报的

options.en: Report it only if the patient or family later asks about it
options.zh: 只有患者或家属事后问起才报

options.en: Note which partner handed you the ampoule for the next performance review
options.zh: 记下是哪位搭档递的安瓿，留到下次绩效评估

questions.explanationEn: A near-miss is a free lesson: the same hole in the system that nearly harmed this patient will line up with someone else's error eventually. Reporting it gives the service the data to change storage, labelling or purchasing, and in a Just Culture it carries no blame — the cross-check working is the system succeeding. Staying silent, or waiting for the patient to ask, forfeits the lesson; blaming the partner punishes the person who was part of the catch. The clinical steps are the same as for any medication error caught in time: do not use the drug, repeat the full check for the correct one, and document. The BC Drug Administration criteria do not deduct for failing to say the rights out loud, but they do grade giving the wrong drug or dose as a major deficiency.
questions.explanationZh: 险肇事件是一堂免费的课：差点伤到这位患者的那个系统漏洞，迟早会和别人的失误排成一线。上报它能让机构拿到改变储存、标签或采购的依据；在公正文化里这不带任何指责——交叉核对起了作用，恰恰说明系统成功了。沉默，或等患者来问，都是白白丢掉这堂课；怪搭档则是惩罚参与了拦截的人。临床步骤和任何及时发现的用药差错一样：不用这支药，对正确的药重新做完整核对，并做记录。BC 给药评分标准不会因为没把「几个正确」说出声而扣分，但给错药或给错剂量会被评为重大缺陷。

questions.questionEn: Your partner is about to spray nitroglycerin into the mouth of a chest-pain patient whose systolic pressure is 100. Which statement represents the 'Alert' level of the PACE graded-assertiveness model?
questions.questionZh: 搭档正要给一位收缩压 100 的胸痛患者喷硝酸甘油。下列哪句话属于 PACE 分级果断表达模型中的「Alert（提醒）」级别？

options.en: 'What was the last blood pressure, and when was it taken?'
options.zh: 「上一次血压是多少，什么时候测的？」

options.en: 'Stop — that is contraindicated. I am not comfortable with this.'
options.zh: 「停——这是禁忌。我不同意这么做。」

options.en: 'I'm concerned — the systolic is 100 and the threshold is 110.'
options.zh: 「我有点担心——收缩压 100，门槛是 110。」

options.en: Taking the spray out of your partner's hand before it is used
options.zh: 在喷雾用出去之前直接从搭档手里拿走

questions.explanationEn: PACE escalates in four steps. Probe is a question that invites the other person to re-check ('What was the last BP?'). Alert states your concern and the fact behind it ('I'm concerned — SBP 100, threshold 110'). Challenge is a direct, unambiguous objection that calls for a stop. Emergency is physical intervention to prevent harm when words have failed. The idea is to start low enough to preserve the relationship but to keep climbing until the risk is addressed — hierarchy never outranks patient safety. The clinical fact is correct: the BC examination guideline contraindicates nitroglycerin when the systolic is below 110 mmHg (and with HR <50 or >150, or recent PDE-5 inhibitor use), so this challenge should prevail.
questions.explanationZh: PACE 分四级递进。Probe（探询）是用提问请对方再核一遍（「上一次血压是多少？」）。Alert（提醒）是说出你的担忧和背后的事实（「我有点担心——收缩压 100，门槛 110」）。Challenge（质疑）是直接、毫不含糊地反对并要求停下。Emergency（紧急）是言语无效时用身体介入防止伤害。思路是从足够低的级别开始以保住关系，但要一级级往上升，直到风险被处理——层级永远压不过患者安全。这里的临床事实是对的：BC 考纲规定收缩压低于 110 mmHg 时禁用硝酸甘油（另有 HR <50 或 >150、近期用过 PDE-5 抑制剂），所以这次质疑应当胜出。

questions.questionEn: Which exchange is a complete closed loop for a medication order during an anaphylaxis call?
questions.questionZh: 在一次过敏性休克的呼叫中，下列哪段对话构成了完整的闭环沟通？

options.en: 'Someone give epi.' — a crew member walks to the drug bag, draws it up and gives it
options.zh: 「谁去给个肾上腺素。」——一名队员走向药箱，抽药并注射

options.en: 'Alex, epi 0.5 mg IM.' — 'Epi 0.5 mg IM.' — 'Correct.' … 'Given, 14:32.'
options.zh: 「Alex，肾上腺素 0.5 mg 肌注。」——「肾上腺素 0.5 mg 肌注。」——「对。」……「已给，14:32。」

options.en: 'Give epi.' — 'OK.' — the partner draws it up and injects it
options.zh: 「给肾上腺素。」——「好。」——搭档抽药并注射

options.en: 'Give epi.' — the partner nods, draws it up and reports it afterwards
options.zh: 「给肾上腺素。」——搭档点头，抽药，事后再报告

questions.explanationEn: A closed loop has three parts: the sender addresses a named person and gives a complete order; the receiver repeats it back (drug, dose, route); the sender confirms the read-back is right. The loop is then closed a second time when the task is reported as done, with the time, so the whole team shares the same picture and nothing is double-dosed or forgotten. An order thrown to the room may be taken by nobody or by two people; 'OK' and a nod give the sender no way to catch a misheard dose or route. The dose quoted is the adult BC dose: epinephrine 1 mg/mL (1:1,000) 0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.5 mg, into the anterolateral thigh, repeatable every 5 minutes up to three times.
questions.explanationZh: 闭环有三个部分：发出者点名并给出完整指令；接收者复述（药、剂量、途径）；发出者确认复述无误。任务完成后再带着时间报告一次，闭环就第二次闭合，全组共享同一幅画面，不会重复给药或遗漏。朝房间喊的指令可能没人接，也可能两个人都去做；「好」和点头让发出者无法发现听错的剂量或途径。题里引用的是 BC 的成人剂量：肾上腺素 1 mg/mL（1:1,000），0.01 mg/kg 肌注、单次最大 0.5 mg，注射于大腿前外侧，每 5 分钟可重复，最多三次。

questions.questionEn: A student notices that her preceptor is about to move a confused diabetic patient without having checked a blood glucose. What does a psychologically safe, flattened-hierarchy crew look like here?
questions.questionZh: 一名实习生注意到带教老师准备在没测血糖的情况下搬动一位意识混乱的糖尿病患者。在心理安全、层级扁平的团队里，这一幕应该是什么样的？

options.en: She waits until after the call so as not to undermine the preceptor in front of the patient
options.zh: 她等到出诊结束再说，免得当着患者的面让老师难堪

options.en: She records the omission in her clinical log for the debrief
options.zh: 她把这个遗漏写进临床日志，留到复盘时说

options.en: She checks the glucose quietly without saying anything to anyone
options.zh: 她悄悄测了血糖，谁也不告诉

options.en: She speaks up now — 'Can we get a glucose first?' — and the preceptor does it
options.zh: 她当场开口——「能先测个血糖吗？」——老师照做

questions.explanationEn: Psychological safety means every crew member, whatever their rank or experience, can raise a concern without fear of ridicule or retaliation — and the senior person's reaction is what makes or breaks it. A flattened hierarchy does not mean nobody leads; it means the leader actively wants to hear the thing they missed. Waiting until afterwards protects egos while the patient goes without a glucose, which the BC Altered Mental Status protocol requires with the baseline vitals. Logging it silently helps no one today. Doing it covertly fixes this patient but leaves the team unable to learn, and it is dishonest about who did what. The PACE 'probe' phrasing used here is the lowest rung and is usually all that is needed when the culture is healthy.
questions.explanationZh: 心理安全意味着每个队员，不论级别和资历，都能提出担忧而不怕被嘲笑或报复——而决定成败的是资深者的反应。层级扁平不是没人领导，而是领导者真心想听到自己漏掉的东西。等事后再说是保全了面子，患者却没测血糖——BC 意识改变协议要求基线生命体征就要包含血糖。默默记日志对今天的患者毫无帮助。偷偷去做虽然救了这一位，但团队学不到东西，而且对「谁做了什么」不诚实。这里用的 PACE「探询」句式是最低一级，在健康的文化里通常这一步就够了。

questions.questionEn: Your partner is on a third IV attempt in a post-ictal patient while snoring respirations have started and nobody has repositioned the airway. Which CRM concept describes the problem?
questions.questionZh: 搭档正在给一位癫痫发作后的患者做第三次静脉穿刺，患者已经出现鼾声呼吸，却没人去调整气道。哪个 CRM 概念描述了这个问题？

options.en: Task fixation — a loss of situational awareness; stop and reassign roles
options.zh: 任务固着——情境意识丧失；停下来重新分工

options.en: Appropriate persistence — IV access is part of the protocol for seizures
options.zh: 恰当的坚持——建立静脉是癫痫协议的一部分

options.en: A closed-loop communication failure between the two of you
options.zh: 你们两人之间的闭环沟通失败

options.en: A documentation problem to note on the PCR
options.zh: 要在 PCR 上记一笔的记录问题

questions.explanationEn: Situational awareness has three levels: perceiving what is happening, understanding what it means, and projecting what will happen next. Fixation collapses all three into a single task — the vein — so the snoring (perception), its meaning (a partially obstructed airway in a patient who cannot protect it) and its trajectory (hypoxia) all go unnoticed. The fix is structural, not heroic: anyone who notices calls it out ('airway is snoring'), the team pauses, the primary survey is re-run and roles are reassigned so the airway has an owner while the IV is deferred or delegated. The BC grading guide would record this as a 100% airway deficiency — 'determines airway problems but fails to act'. Closed-loop communication is about orders, and documentation is about what is written down afterwards.
questions.explanationZh: 情境意识有三个层次：察觉正在发生什么、理解它意味着什么、预判接下来会怎样。任务固着把三者全部压缩到一件事——那根血管——上，于是鼾声（察觉）、它的含义（不能保护气道的患者出现部分气道梗阻）、它的走向（缺氧）全都被忽略。解决办法靠结构而不靠英雄：谁注意到就喊出来（「气道有鼾声」），全组暂停，重跑初级评估，重新分工让气道有专人负责、静脉穿刺推后或交给别人。BC 评分指南会把这记为 100% 的气道缺陷——「发现气道问题却不采取行动」。闭环沟通说的是指令，记录说的是事后写下来的东西。

questions.questionEn: You are the team leader at a cardiac arrest with your partner and three firefighters. In CRM terms, what should your role look like?
questions.questionZh: 你是一次心脏骤停现场的团队领导，身边有搭档和三名消防员。按 CRM 的说法，你的角色应该是什么样？

options.en: Do the compressions yourself, because high-quality compressions matter most
options.zh: 自己做按压，因为高质量按压最重要

options.en: Stay silent so the others can concentrate on their tasks
options.zh: 保持安静，让其他人专心各自的任务

options.en: Step back, keep the overview, assign roles and run closed-loop orders
options.zh: 退后一步掌握全局，分配角色，指令走闭环

options.en: Hand leadership to whoever is doing compressions every two minutes
options.zh: 每两分钟把领导权交给正在按压的人

questions.explanationEn: A leader buried in a task loses the overview — the same fixation problem in a different form. With five people available, the leader's job is to stand where the whole scene is visible, assign compressors, airway and AED roles, call the two-minute rotations so compressions stay high quality with pauses under 5 seconds, run the reversible-causes checklist aloud, and keep every instruction closed-loop. If the team is only two, the leader must do hands-on work, but still owns the plan. Silence removes the shared mental model; rotating leadership with the compressors destroys continuity. The AET course drills these arrest roles in its high-performance CPR weekend; the BC guideline's expectations are 30:2 adult CPR with minimal interruption and AED analysis as soon as available.
questions.explanationZh: 埋头做事的领导会失去全局——这是同一个固着问题的另一种形式。有五个人可用时，领导的工作是站在能看见全场的位置，分配按压、气道和 AED 角色，喊出两分钟轮换以保持高质量按压、中断少于 5 秒，大声过一遍可逆原因清单，并让每一条指令都走闭环。如果只有两个人，领导必须亲自动手，但依然掌握计划。沉默会让共同认知消失；跟着按压者轮换领导权则毁掉连续性。AET 课程在高效能 CPR 周末专门演练这些骤停角色；BC 考纲的要求是成人 30:2、尽量少中断、AED 一到就分析。

questions.questionEn: En route you realize you gave dimenhydrinate 50 mg IV to a frail 86-year-old who weighs 40 kg — the BC dose is 1 mg/kg to a maximum of 50 mg, so 40 mg was the limit. She is drowsy but stable. What is the correct sequence of actions?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中你意识到给一位体重 40 公斤、86 岁的虚弱老人静脉推了茶苯海明 50 mg——BC 剂量是 1 mg/kg、最多 50 mg，所以上限本该是 40 mg。她有些嗜睡但病情稳定。正确的处理顺序是什么？

options.en: Amend the PCR to show the intended 40 mg so the record is consistent
options.zh: 把 PCR 改成本来打算给的 40 mg，让记录一致

options.en: Reassess her, then disclose, hand over the real dose, document and report
options.zh: 先复评她，再告知、如实交接剂量、记录并上报

options.en: Wait to see whether any harm develops before mentioning it to anyone
options.zh: 先等等看会不会出问题，再决定要不要告诉任何人

options.en: Tell only your partner, since the overdose was small and she remains stable
options.zh: 只告诉搭档，反正超量不多，她也还稳定

questions.explanationEn: Patient safety comes first: reassess ABCs, LOC and vitals, because an antihistamine overshoot in a small, elderly patient can deepen sedation — the BC monograph lists the elderly among dimenhydrinate's cautions. Then honesty — the patient has a right to know what was given to her body, the receiving team must know the real dose to interpret her drowsiness, and the PCR must record what actually happened; altering a record to hide an error is falsification, which the AET glossary notes can cost a licence. Finally, the incident report feeds the Just Culture process: a 25% overshoot from not weight-adjusting is most likely human error or at-risk behaviour, and the learning is for everyone. Waiting for harm, or keeping it inside the crew, removes the hospital's ability to watch for it and turns a small error into a concealment.
questions.explanationZh: 患者安全第一：复评 ABC、意识和生命体征，因为体重小的老人抗组胺药超量会加深镇静——BC 药物专论把老年人列在茶苯海明的注意事项里。然后是诚实——患者有权知道自己身体里被给了什么，接收团队必须知道真实剂量才能解读她的嗜睡，PCR 必须记录实际发生的事；为掩盖差错而改记录是伪造，AET 术语表提醒这可能丢掉执照。最后，事件报告进入公正文化的流程：没按体重调整导致的 25% 超量，多半是人为失误或冒险行为，教训是给所有人的。等出了问题再说，或只在组内消化，都剥夺了医院观察的机会，把一个小差错变成了隐瞒。

questions.questionEn: At handover the triage nurse says flatly, 'This isn't a stroke, he's just drunk.' You disagree. Which response reflects CRM and interprofessional respect?
questions.questionZh: 交接时分诊护士直截了当地说：「这不是卒中，他就是喝多了。」你不同意。哪种回应体现了 CRM 和跨专业的尊重？

options.en: 'I was on scene and you weren't, so I know better than you do.'
options.zh: 「我在现场，你不在，我比你清楚。」

options.en: Withhold the rest of your findings until a physician arrives to hear them
options.zh: 把剩下的发现留着，等医生来了再说

options.en: Leave quickly to avoid an argument and let the chart speak
options.zh: 赶紧走，别吵起来，让病历自己说话

options.en: Acknowledge her view, give your SBAR findings, ask what she is seeing
options.zh: 肯定她的看法，用 SBAR 给出发现，问她看到了什么

questions.explanationEn: Respect between disciplines means treating the other person's expertise as real while advocating for your patient with facts rather than status. A structured SBAR handover — situation, background, the objective assessment, your recommendation — moves the discussion from opinion to data: a documented last-known-well time, a positive FAST-VAN and a normal glucose make 'just drunk' hard to sustain, and the BC Stroke protocol requires exactly those elements. Asking what she sees keeps the loop open in case she is right. Pulling rank damages the relationship and does not help the patient; withholding information or leaving abandons him. If she still disagrees and you believe he is at risk, graded assertiveness continues up the chain, calmly, until a physician assesses him.
questions.explanationZh: 跨专业的尊重，是把对方的专业能力当真，同时用事实而不是身份为患者发声。结构化的 SBAR 交接——现状、背景、客观评估、你的建议——把讨论从观点拉回数据：有记录的最后正常时间、阳性的 FAST-VAN、正常的血糖，让「就是喝多了」很难站得住，而 BC 卒中协议要求的恰恰是这些要素。问她看到了什么，是让回路保持开放，以防她才是对的。摆资历会伤害关系，对患者没有帮助；扣住信息或一走了之，是把患者丢下。如果她仍不同意而你认为患者有风险，就冷静地沿分级果断表达往上走，直到有医生来评估他。

questions.questionEn: Under BC's Child, Family and Community Service Act, what is the threshold at which a paramedic must report a concern about a child?
questions.questionZh: 按 BC 省《儿童、家庭和社区服务法》（CFCSA），急救员对儿童的担忧达到什么程度就必须上报？

options.en: Only after a physician has confirmed that the injuries are non-accidental
options.zh: 只有在医生确认伤情并非意外之后

options.en: Only when the child directly discloses abuse to you
options.zh: 只有在孩子亲口向你说出被虐待时

options.en: Reason to believe the child needs protection — no proof required
options.zh: 有理由相信孩子需要保护——不需要证据

options.en: Only with the consent of the parent or legal guardian
options.zh: 只有在家长或法定监护人同意时

questions.explanationEn: Section 14 of the Act requires anyone who has reason to believe a child (under 19 in BC) needs protection to promptly report to a child protection worker (the Ministry of Children and Family Development, via its 24-hour line, or police if the child is in immediate danger). The reporter does not investigate, does not need proof, and does not need anyone's permission; the duty overrides confidentiality (only solicitor-client privilege is exempt), a good-faith report is protected from liability, and failing to report is an offence. Waiting for a physician or for a disclosure is exactly the delay the statute was written to prevent. The paramedic's job is to care for the child, note objective findings and quotes, and make the call.
questions.explanationZh: 该法第 14 条规定，任何人只要有理由相信某个儿童（BC 省指 19 岁以下）需要保护，就必须尽快向儿童保护工作者报告（儿童与家庭发展厅的 24 小时热线，孩子有即刻危险时报警）。报告者不负责调查、不需要证据、也不需要任何人的许可；这项义务高于保密义务（只有律师-当事人特权例外），善意报告受法律保护，不报告则构成违法。等医生确认或等孩子开口，正是这部法律想要防止的拖延。急救员的任务是照顾好孩子、记下客观发现和原话，然后打这个电话。

questions.questionEn: You hand over a 4-year-old with patterned bruises of different ages to the emergency department and tell the nurse you are worried. Has your legal duty under the CFCSA been met?
questions.questionZh: 你把一名身上有不同时期、带形状瘀斑的 4 岁幼儿交接给急诊科，并告诉护士你很担心。你在 CFCSA 下的法律义务履行了吗？

options.en: No — the duty is personal; telling hospital staff does not discharge it
options.zh: 没有——这项义务是个人的；告诉医院人员不能免除

options.en: Yes — once the hospital has the child, the responsibility passes to their team
options.zh: 履行了——孩子一到医院，责任就转给他们的团队

options.en: Yes — as long as the concern is written clearly on the PCR
options.zh: 履行了——只要把担忧清楚地写进 PCR

options.en: No — you must first confront the parent and hear their explanation
options.zh: 没有——你必须先当面质问家长、听他们解释

questions.explanationEn: The Act places the duty on each person who forms the belief; it is not transferred by handing the patient to another professional, and a verbal worry at triage can be lost in a busy department. The safe practice is to make the report yourself (and tell the hospital you have done so), to document the objective findings and any verbatim statements, and to follow your employer's notification policy. Documentation alone is not a report. Confronting the suspected abuser is not required, can escalate danger to the child, and may compromise a later investigation — your questions are limited to what you need for care, and you stay neutral and non-accusatory with the family.
questions.explanationZh: 法律把义务放在每一个形成这种判断的人身上；把患者交给另一位专业人员并不能转移义务，而分诊台上一句口头的担心在繁忙的科室里很容易丢失。稳妥的做法是自己报告（并告诉医院你已经报了），记录客观发现和任何原话，并遵守雇主的通报流程。只做记录不等于报告。当面质问疑似施虐者不是法律要求，可能加大孩子的危险，还可能妨碍日后的调查——你的提问只限于照护所需，对家属保持中立、不带指责。

questions.questionEn: An 84-year-old with dementia has unexplained bruises and lives in a filthy home; the caregiver is dismissive. In BC, what is the framework for reporting concerns about a vulnerable adult?
questions.questionZh: 一位 84 岁的失智老人身上有原因不明的瘀斑，家里肮脏不堪；照护者态度敷衍。在 BC 省，对弱势成人的担忧该通过什么框架报告？

options.en: The CFCSA applies to all vulnerable people, so the same mandatory report is made to MCFD
options.zh: CFCSA 适用于所有弱势人群，所以同样向 MCFD 做强制报告

options.en: Only the police may be notified, and only with the adult's consent
options.zh: 只能报警，而且必须得到老人本人同意

options.en: No report is possible without the adult's consent or a court order
options.zh: 没有老人同意或法院命令就不能报告

options.en: The Adult Guardianship Act — anyone may report to a designated agency; it is not a legal duty
options.zh: 《成人监护法》——任何人都可以向指定机构报告；这不是法定义务

questions.explanationEn: BC's Adult Guardianship Act (Part 3) covers adults who are abused or neglected and unable to seek support because of a disability, illness or restraint. Reporting is permissive rather than mandatory — the statute says a person 'may' report — but health-care professional standards and employer policies treat it as the expected action, the report may be made without the adult's consent, and a good-faith reporter is protected from liability. Reports go to a designated agency: the regional health authorities (and Community Living BC for its clients), with police involved where a crime is suspected or the adult is in immediate danger. The CFCSA applies only to children. The clinical priority is unchanged: assess and treat the injuries, take the glucose and temperature an unwell older adult needs, and document objectively.
questions.explanationZh: BC 省《成人监护法》第三部分针对的是因残疾、疾病或被限制而无法自行寻求帮助、遭受虐待或忽视的成人。报告是允许性而非强制性的——法律用的是「可以」报告——但医疗专业标准和雇主政策都把它当作应有的行动，报告不需要成人本人同意，善意报告者免于法律责任。报告对象是指定机构：各区域卫生局（CLBC 负责其自己的服务对象），怀疑犯罪或老人有即刻危险时报警介入。CFCSA 只适用于儿童。临床优先级不变：评估处理伤情，给身体不适的老人测血糖和体温，客观记录。

questions.questionEn: Which statement about BC's Gunshot and Stab Wound Disclosure Act is correct?
questions.questionZh: 关于 BC 省《枪伤与刺伤披露法》，哪一项说法正确？

options.en: Paramedics must obtain a statement from the patient about who caused the wound
options.zh: 急救员必须向患者问清是谁造成的伤

options.en: The facility tells police the name, the wound and the facility location
options.zh: 医疗机构告知警方：姓名、伤情种类、机构地点

options.en: Every stab wound, including accidental and self-inflicted ones, must be disclosed
options.zh: 所有刺伤，包括意外和自伤造成的，都必须披露

options.en: Disclosure requires the patient's written consent or a warrant
options.zh: 披露需要患者的书面同意或搜查令

questions.explanationEn: The Act obliges the treating health care facility — not the individual clinician — to disclose a narrow set of facts to the local police: the person's name if known, the fact that they are being treated for a gunshot or stab wound, and the facility's name and location. Stab wounds are excluded when they are self-inflicted or unintentional. Disclosure must not delay or interfere with treatment, consent is not required, and the facility is protected for disclosing in good faith. It does not turn the paramedic into an investigator: your contribution is accurate, objective documentation of the wound and the circumstances as told to you (in quotation marks), preservation of clothing and evidence where care allows, and a complete handover so the facility can meet its obligation.
questions.explanationZh: 这部法律要求的是接诊的医疗机构——而不是个人——向当地警方披露一组很窄的事实：患者姓名（若已知）、正在因枪伤或刺伤接受治疗这一事实、机构名称和地点。自伤或无意造成的刺伤不在披露范围内。披露不得延误或干扰治疗，不需要患者同意，机构因善意披露受法律保护。它并没有把急救员变成调查者：你的贡献是对伤口和患者所述经过（用引号记原话）做准确、客观的记录，在不影响救治的前提下保护衣物和证据，并做完整交接，让机构能履行它的义务。

questions.questionEn: A stable stabbing victim needs his shirt removed to expose and dress the wound. Which approach preserves evidence without compromising care?
questions.questionZh: 一位病情稳定的刺伤患者需要脱掉衬衫以暴露并包扎伤口。哪种做法既保护了证据又不影响救治？

options.en: Cut straight through the hole in the fabric — it is the fastest route to the wound
options.zh: 沿布料上的破口直接剪开——这是到达伤口最快的路

options.en: Shake the shirt out to check for weapons, then fold it into a plastic bag
options.zh: 把衬衫抖一抖检查有没有武器，再叠好放进塑料袋

options.en: Cut along the seams away from the defect; bag each garment separately in paper
options.zh: 沿衣缝、避开破口剪开；每件衣物分开装纸袋

options.en: Discard the clothing to reduce contamination of the ambulance
options.zh: 把衣物扔掉，减少对救护车的污染

questions.explanationEn: The defect in the fabric records the weapon's size, shape and angle, and the surrounding cloth carries blood, fibre and residue; cutting through it destroys that record, and shaking the garment sheds trace evidence. Paper bags breathe — plastic traps moisture and lets biological evidence degrade. Each item stays separate so that transfer between garments cannot be alleged later, and the chain of custody is kept simple by handing items to police or to the receiving facility with a note of who held them. None of this ever outranks patient care: if the patient were unstable you would expose the chest the fastest way you could and simply document what you did and why. The AET module's principle is 'care first, then preserve what you can'.
questions.explanationZh: 布料上的破口记录着凶器的大小、形状和角度，周围的布带着血迹、纤维和残留物；从破口剪过去就毁了这份记录，抖衣服会把微量证据抖掉。纸袋透气——塑料袋会闷住湿气，让生物证据降解。每件衣物分开装，是为了日后没人能说证据在衣物之间发生了转移；把物品交给警方或接收机构并记下经手人，证据链就简单清楚。这一切永远不高于患者救治：如果患者不稳定，你就用最快的方法暴露胸部，然后记录你做了什么、为什么。AET 模块的原则是「先救治，再尽可能保全」。

questions.questionEn: You find an adult with rigor mortis and dependent lividity on the floor of a locked apartment; a knife lies beside the body and police have not yet arrived. The scene is otherwise safe. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你在一间反锁的公寓地板上发现一名已出现尸僵和坠积性尸斑的成人；尸体旁有一把刀，警方尚未到达。现场其他方面是安全的。你该怎么做？

options.en: Confirm death with minimal disturbance, leave everything, and brief police
options.zh: 以最小扰动确认死亡，一切原位不动，向警方交代

options.en: Move the knife into your kit so nobody is hurt, and note where it was
options.zh: 把刀收进器材箱以免伤人，并记下它原来的位置

options.en: Roll the body to look for a wallet and identification for the coroner
options.zh: 翻动尸体找钱包和身份证件，方便法医

options.en: Tidy the room so the family does not have to see it like this when they arrive
options.zh: 把房间收拾一下，别让家属到了看到这个样子

questions.explanationEn: Rigor and dependent lividity are obvious-death findings, so resuscitation is not started and the scene becomes a potential crime scene. Your footprints, the door you opened and the one light you switched on are now part of the record, so you limit movement to what confirming death required, use a single path in and out, touch nothing else, and give police a precise account. A weapon is moved only if it poses a real danger — and then its original position is noted and reported. Identification, personal effects and the position of the body belong to the police and coroner; under BC's Coroners Act a death that is sudden, unexpected or possibly from violence must be reported, which BCEHS does through its dispatch and police. Tidying destroys evidence, and the family's distress is addressed by compassionate communication, not by altering the scene. Obvious-death criteria also appear in the BC guideline's cardiac arrest section as reasons not to begin CPR.
questions.explanationZh: 尸僵和坠积性尸斑属于明显死亡的表现，所以不启动复苏，现场也随之成为潜在的犯罪现场。你的脚印、你开过的门、你按亮的那盏灯现在都是记录的一部分，所以把活动限制在确认死亡所必需的范围内，进出走同一条路线，别的什么都不碰，并向警方精确交代。只有在武器确实构成危险时才移动它——并且要记下并报告它原来的位置。身份证件、随身物品和尸体的位置归警方和法医处理；按 BC 省《法医法》，突然、意外或可能由暴力导致的死亡必须报告，BCEHS 通过调度和警方完成。收拾房间会毁掉证据；家属的悲痛要靠有同理心的沟通来回应，而不是改变现场。明显死亡的标准也出现在 BC 考纲心脏骤停章节里，作为不开始 CPR 的理由。

questions.questionEn: While you dress a burn on a 6-year-old's hand, she says, 'Daddy held it on the stove.' How should this be documented?
questions.questionZh: 你给一名 6 岁女孩手上的烧伤包扎时，她说：「爸爸把我的手按在炉子上。」这该怎么记录？

options.en: Paraphrase it as 'alleged abuse by father' in the narrative
options.zh: 在叙述里改写成「疑似父亲虐待」

options.en: Leave it out — young children are unreliable witnesses
options.zh: 不写——小孩子的话不可靠

options.en: Write 'child abuse confirmed' so the hospital social worker acts quickly on arrival
options.zh: 写「已确认儿童虐待」，好让医院社工到院后尽快行动

options.en: Quote her verbatim, attributed; describe the burn without naming a cause
options.zh: 逐字引用她的原话并注明出处；描述烧伤但不写原因

questions.explanationEn: A spontaneous statement from a child, recorded exactly as spoken and attributed, is the most valuable thing the record can contain — paraphrase changes meaning and a label like 'alleged abuse' is an opinion, not an observation. The injury is described as you see it: '3 × 4 cm partial-thickness burn, palmar surface of left hand, sharply demarcated edge, no splash marks', leaving the interpretation to the forensic team. Do not interview the child further or ask leading questions; the forensic interview is done once, by trained specialists, and well-meant questioning can contaminate it. Omitting the statement withholds evidence; declaring abuse 'confirmed' overstates what you know. And the statement gives you reason to believe she needs protection, so the CFCSA report is made in addition to the documentation.
questions.explanationZh: 孩子自发说出的话，原样记录并注明出处，是病历里最有价值的内容——改写会改变含义，而「疑似虐待」这样的标签是观点，不是观察。伤情按你看到的样子描述：「左手掌面 3 × 4 cm 部分皮层烧伤，边缘整齐，无飞溅痕迹」，解读留给法医团队。不要继续追问孩子，也不要提引导性问题；法证访谈由受过训练的专业人员只做一次，好心的追问可能污染它。不写这句话是扣留证据；宣称虐待「已确认」则夸大了你所知道的。另外，这句话已经让你有理由相信她需要保护，所以除了记录之外还要做 CFCSA 报告。

questions.questionEn: An adult who reports being sexually assaulted an hour ago asks whether she can shower before going to the hospital. What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一位成年女性说自己一小时前遭到性侵，问去医院前能不能先洗个澡。最佳回应是什么？

options.en: Tell her she must not shower because the assault has to be reported to police
options.zh: 告诉她不能洗澡，因为性侵必须报警

options.en: Explain what preserves evidence, then respect whatever she decides
options.zh: 解释怎样能保全证据，然后尊重她的任何决定

options.en: Tell her evidence is only collected by police, so what she does now does not matter
options.zh: 告诉她证据只能由警察采集，所以她现在做什么都无所谓

options.en: Collect her clothing yourself and bag it as evidence for the police
options.zh: 由你亲自收走她的衣物装袋，作为证据交警方

questions.explanationEn: An adult survivor decides for herself whether to involve police — there is no mandatory report for a competent adult, and taking that choice away repeats the loss of control at the heart of the assault. Your role is to give her the information she needs to keep her options open (evidence is best collected within hours; washing, changing, voiding and eating all reduce it), to offer transport to a hospital with a forensic nurse examiner or sexual assault service, to provide a same-gender attendant if she wishes, and to document her words and visible injuries objectively. Forensic collection is done by trained examiners with her consent, not by paramedics; clothing is handled only if she removes it and then kept in paper. Trauma-informed care — asking permission before touching, explaining each step, believing her — is both the humane and the evidentially sound approach.
questions.explanationZh: 成年受害者自己决定是否报警——对有行为能力的成人没有强制报告，剥夺这个选择等于重演性侵核心的那种失控感。你的角色是提供让她保留选择余地所需的信息（证据最好在几小时内采集；洗澡、换衣、排尿、进食都会减少证据），提出送她去有法医护士或性侵服务的医院，她愿意的话安排同性别的随车人员，并客观记录她的原话和可见的伤。法证采集由受过训练的检查人员在她同意下进行，不是急救员的事；衣物只有在她自己脱下时才经手，并用纸袋保存。创伤知情的照护——触碰前先征得同意、每一步都解释、相信她——既是人道的做法，也是在证据上最稳妥的做法。
